summary: Masato Kobayashi is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona. He served as a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from circa 2000 to 2002.

Masatoshi Konishi (1938–2020) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1957 to 1965. He later held a post at Rikkyo University from circa 1972 to 2004.
Masatoshi Nagatomi (1926–2000) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and Harvard University, where he later served as a professor from circa 1969 to 1996.

Masayuki Taira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. After studying at Kyoto University, he held posts at Kansai University (circa 1983–1989), Osaka University (circa 1989–2017), and Kyoto Tachibana University (circa 2017–2022).
Masumi Mochizuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served at Minobusan University, where he was attested as a Faculty of Buddhism lecturer in 2001 and as a professor in 2015.

Mathieu Boisvert works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth, founded the Groupe de recherches interdisciplinaire sur le Montréal ethno-religieux, and became a professor at Université du Québec à Montréal in 1992.

Matthew B. Orsborn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisors Guang Xing and Y. Karunadasa, alongside traditional teachers Hsing Yun and Huishang (all attested 2012).
Matthew Immergut is a religious studies scholar who studied under Culadasa. In 2011, he was attested as an Associate Professor of Sociology at the State University of New York at Purchase.

Matthew King is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Kunga Sherab and teacher Thupten Champa, completing his PhD at the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett by 2014.

Matthew R. Sayers is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle, and held an attested post at Lebanon Valley College in 2013.

Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaii under Helen J. Baroni and Michel Mohr, and completed his PhD at Duke University under Richard M. Jaffe.

Matthew T. Kapstein is a Tibetologist and philosopher who earned his PhD from Brown University. He held positions at the University of Chicago, Columbia University, and served as Director of Tibetan Religious Studies at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Matthias von Lexer (1830–1892) was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at the University of Freiburg (circa 1864–1868), University of Würzburg (circa 1868–1874), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (circa 1874–1892).

Matthieu Ricard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed a PhD at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob and studied under traditional teacher Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche from circa 1972 to 1991.

Mattia Salvini is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and held posts at the International Buddhist College and Mahidol University.

Mauli Chand Prasad is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He wrote a doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University supervised by B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna, and served as a Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Maurice Bloomfield (1855–1928) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under William Dwight Whitney and Charles Rockwell Lanman, earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins University, and was appointed professor there in 1881.

Maurice O'Connell Walshe (1911–1998) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Walpola Rahula. He held a post at the Institute of Germanic and Romance Studies from circa 1955 to 1979.
Maurice Wiles (1923–2005) was a religious studies scholar. He attended Tonbridge School and studied at Christ's College, Cambridge from circa 1945 to 1948.
Maurine Stuart (1922–1990) was a Buddhist studies figure who attended the University of Manitoba from circa 1939 to 1943. She studied under traditional teachers Hakuun Yasutani and Eido Tai Shimano.
